note: Colosseum set dressing for the Proving Floor / Proving Grounds arena. Phase 0 art direction (owner): a ceremonial duelling platform ringed by spectators — standing stone where the map has walls, rough gladiatorial cover where it has cover. Each role is a LIST of interchangeable variants; the board picks one per tile by a hash of the square, so a run is no longer the same mesh repeated. Everything is authored in TILES and placed 1:1 — a wall prop is exactly WALL_HEIGHT (0.9) tall, a cover prop exactly COVER_HEIGHT (0.45) — so a prop cannot change what a square reads as. Colours are neutral stone and dark wood: MAP_PIPELINE §4 forbids a permanent fixture landing in a saturated UI colour family, and greys (r≈g≈b) and dark wood (every channel well under 130) sit clear of the amber AoE and the team hues. ORIENTATION of cover is NOT set here: the map authors a per-tile `facing` (COVER-EDGE) and the renderer sits the barricade on that edge and turns it along the boundary, stretched to crouch height. Walls have no facing and take a hashed quarter-turn per tile for variety.

variants.comment: The standing fluted column: square plinth, tapered fluted shaft, flared capital.
A broken column: no capital, the shaft snapped short and uneven, fallen chunks at the base. Reads as a ruin but still fills the wall square.
A heavy, squat column — thicker shaft, deeper flutes, a broad plinth and capital. Weight and variety next to the slender fluted one.
The rough wooden stake barricade: four uneven stakes lashed to a crossbar between two heavier posts.
A denser, taller barricade — five stakes and a higher crossbar. A heavier stretch of the same fence line.
A stone block / low altar: a broad base course with a narrower slab on top. Masonry cover between the wooden stretches.
